overview: Pueblo societies comprise distinct communities and histories. Chaco Canyon and Mesa Verde preserve ancestral building and farming landscapes; Taos Pueblo is a living community with its own traditions and government.

items.text: At Chaco, builders planned multistory Great Houses whose construction could span generations. Their masonry and shared layouts mark a regional architectural tradition.
Many Chaco structures were oriented toward solar, lunar or cardinal directions. Their placement linked buildings to a meaningful surrounding landscape.
Mesa Verde preserves farming terraces, check dams, reservoirs and ditches as well as houses. These remains document the engineering of everyday subsistence.
Roads connected Chaco Great Houses across the region. Some major buildings may have hosted periodic ceremonies and exchange rather than dense permanent populations.
At Taos, families maintain adobe homes by renewing earthen plaster. Taos describes that work as an ongoing connection between ancestors and the present.
Changes in ancestral settlements did not end Pueblo life. Mesa Verde remains a living connection to present-day Pueblo peoples, and Taos continues as a sovereign community.
